record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: What is the smallest degree d such that the Gorenstein locus Hilb^Gor_d(A^4), the open locus in Hilb_d(A^4) parameterizing Gorenstein algebras, is reducible? The paper records the bounds 15 <= d <= 140.

evidence.quote: Problem VI. What is the smallest d such that HilbGor_d(A^4) is reducible? We have 15 <= d <= 140.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parameterizing zero-dimensional closed subschemes of length $d$ in the affine space $\mathbb{A}^4_k$. Inside $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$ consider the open subscheme
$$\mathrm{Hilb}^{\mathrm{Gor}}_d(\mathbb{A}^4) \subset \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$$
parameterizing those subschemes $Z \subset \mathbb{A}^4$ whose structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_Z$ is a Gorenstein $k$-algebra (equivalently, every local ring $\mathcal{O}_{Z,p}$ is Gorenstein). Determine the smallest positive integer $d$ for which $\mathrm{Hilb}^{\mathrm{Gor}}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$ is reducible. It is known that this minimal $d$ satisfies $15 \le d \le 140$; find its exact value (or improve the bounds).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is recorded as open with the bounds 15 ≤ d ≤ 140 in the problem list on deformations of Artinian algebras and Hilbert schemes. Casnati–Jelisiejew–Notari (2015) established irreducibility for low degrees, and subsequent work has produced new elementary components for the Gorenstein locus, but the exact threshold for reducibility of the Gorenstein locus on A^4 does not appear to have been pinned down in the literature available through search.

status_evidence.title: Irreducibility of the Gorenstein loci of Hilbert schemes via ray families
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes irreducibility of Gorenstein loci of Hilbert schemes in low degree via ray families (Casnati, Jelisiejew, Notari).
status_evidence.claim: Known irreducibility results determine the lower bound regime but do not determine the threshold on A^4.

status_evidence.title: New elementary components of the Gorenstein locus of the Hilbert scheme of points
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs new elementary components of the Gorenstein locus of the Hilbert scheme of points, contributing to upper bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides reducibility witnesses giving upper bounds but does not match the lower bound.
